text:
ana: FYI — AcmePro (org:7890) just hit a big wave of 429s after we turned on rl-enforce-v2 enforcement yesterday. Customer says 20k 429s in ~15m during their nightly import job.
jasper: thx. are they on standard tier? any repro steps or headers from their side?
ana: they are standard. customer pasted this header snapshot: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 30
Content-Type: application/json
```
ana: and their minimal repro curl (redacted token):
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input": "...bulk import chunk..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
maggie: seeing the same spike in canary telemetry — 2x 429 rate in the 5% canary pool after the enforcement flag went live. Seems burst handling got much stricter.
jasper: rl-enforce-v2 is controlled by FF service (ff:rl-enforce-v2). Canary % = 5. Current enforcement switches to hard quota checks for short bursts. Possible mitigations: 1) flip canary to 0% to stop enforcement rollout, 2) increase per-customer temporary quota, 3) relax burst_window/token refill for enforcement policy. Thoughts?
tom: if we flip to 0% we stop new enforcement for everyone in canary but traffic already hit 429s — flipping should reduce new 429s. Risk: we revert to previous lenient behavior which allowed extra tokens. If AcmePro still has backlog they may resubmit and we could see transient surge. Recommend also giving them a one-time +5000 token bump for 30m.
leah-billing: emergency token bump is fine from billing side for customer experience; will log a credit and notify acct team. confirm amount and duration.
jasper: I can flip flag now. command (internal):
```
POST https://flags.internal/api/v1/flags/rl-enforce-v2
body: {"percentage":0}
# response: {"flag":"rl-enforce-v2","percentage":0}
```
sre-bot: Deploy 2935104400 applied rl-enforce-v2=5% at 2026-03-17T10:00:00Z
jasper: running update...
sre-bot: OK: rl-enforce-v2 set to 0% by jasper (req 2935104520)
nana: AcmePro says errors dropped to near zero within ~60s, they're resuming import. thank you.
maggie: nice. I'll keep the canary metrics streaming for 30m. if 429s resurface, we rollback enforcement globally and file postmortem. Also propose we change default enforcement config: burst_window from 2s -> 8s and prefetch KV cache allowance for imports.
jasper: logging action items: 1) temp +5000 tokens for org:7890 for 30m (leah to note billing), 2) revert ff to 0% (done), 3) schedule config tweak PR to relax burst_window and add gradual ramp (eng-platform), 4) postmortem if needed.
leah-billing: noted. I created billing ticket BL-8123 and set emergency credit flag.
tom: can we add a small health-check in canary that simulates a 500-request burst to validate enforcement thresholds before next rollout?
maggie: yes, add synthetic burst test to canary pipeline, run after config PR lands.
nana: customer confirmed job completed. I'll keep monitoring with them for 2h and will escalate if anything else. :thumbsup:
